VIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|311}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpõ Tuesday in vvhitsunvveeke. And in a votiue of the Holy Ghost.}}And vvhen the Apostles vvho vvere in Hierusalem, had heard that Samaria had receiued the vvord of God: they {{sup|‖}} sent vnto them {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Sæpe sibi socium Petrus facit esse Ioannem: Ecclesiæ quia virgo placet.'' Peter often maketh John his companion, because the Church loveth a virgin. Arator apud Bedam in Act.}}∷ Peter & Iohn. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}}† Vvho vvhen they vvere come, praied for them, that they might receiue the holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}}† For he vvas not yet come vpon any of them, but they vvere only baptized in the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}}† Then {{sup|‖}} did they impose their handes vpon them, {{sup|‖}} and they receiued the holy Ghost.⊣ {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}}† And vvhen Simon had seen that by the imposition of the hand of the Apostles, the holy Ghost vvas giuen, he {{sup|‖}} offered them money, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}}† saying, Giue me also this povver, that on vvhomsoeuer I impose my handes, he may receiue the holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† But Peter said to him, Thy money be vvith thee vnto perdition: because thou hast thought that the gift of God is purchased vvith money. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}}† Thou hast no part, nor lot in this vvord. For thy hart is not right before God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=22}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''μετανόησον ἀπὸ See Apocal. 9, 21.''}}∷ {{sup|‖}} Doe penance therfore from this thy vvickednesse: and pray to God, {{sup|‖}} if perhaps this cogitation of thy hart may be remitted thee. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=23}}† For I see thou art in the gall of bitternes and the obligation of iniquitie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=24}}† And Simon ansvvering said, {{sup|‖}} Pray you for me to our Lord, that nothing come vpon me of these things vvhich you haue said. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=25}}† And they in deede hauing testified and spoken the vvord of our Lord, returned to Hierusalem, and euangelized to many countries of the Samaritans.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=26}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle vpon Thursday in Easter vveeke.}}∷ And an Angel of our Lord spake to Philippe, saying: Arise, and goe tovvard the South, to the vvay that goeth dovvne from Hierusalem into Gaza: th{{sup|‖}} is is desert. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=27}}† And rising he vvent. And behold, a man of Æthiopia, an eunuch, of great authoritie vnder Candáce the Queene of the Æthiopians, vvho vvas ouer al her treasures, vvas come to Hierusalem {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note that this Æthiopian came to Hierusalem to adore, that is, on Pilgrimage. vvhere by vve may learne that it is an acceptable acte of religion to go from home to places of greater deuotiõ & sanctificatiõ.}}∷ to adore: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=28}}† and he vvas returning and sitting vpon his chariot, and reading Esay the prophet. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=29}}† And the Spirit said to Philippe, Goe neere, and ioyne thy self to this same chariot. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=30}}† And Philippe running therevnto, heard him reading Esay the prophet, and he said: Trovvest thou that thou vnderstandest the things vvhich thou readest? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=31}}† Vvho said, And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Scriptures are so vvritten that they can not be vnderstood vvithout an interpreter, as easy as our Protestants make them. See S. Hierom ''Ep. ad Paulinũ de omnibus diuinæ historiæ libris'', set in the beginning of latin bibles.}}∷ hovv can I, vnlesse some man shevv me? & he desired Philippe that he vvould come vp and sit vvith him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=32}}† And the place of the scripture vvhich he did reade, vvas this: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Es. 53, 7.''}}* ''As a sheepe to slaughter vvas he led: and as a lambe before his shearer, vvithout voice, so did he not open his mouth''. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=33}}† ''In humilitie his iudgement vvas taken avvay.''<noinclude>{{rh|||His}}</noinclude>
